chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever divorces [his wife] three times in one session while she is in a state of purity (or specifically, not in a state of purity as per the command), it is not [valid]. The divorce is only that which Allah, Exalted and Mighty, commanded. So whoever goes against it, there is no divorce for him. And indeed, Ibn Umar divorced his wife three times in one session while she was menstruating, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered him to marry her and not to count the divorce [as valid].'

He said: 'And a man came to Ali (peace be upon him) and said: O Commander of the Faithful, I have divorced my wife. He said: Do you have a witness/testimony? He said: No. He said: Go back to your wife (or remain separated/uncouple).'

key_terms.ابْنُ عُمَرَ: Ibn Umar, a companion of the Prophet
key_terms.اعْزُبْ: Go back/remain separated (a term used by Imam Ali regarding the validity of the divorce)
key_terms.عَلَى غَيْرِ طُهْرٍ: While not in a state of purity (specifically during menstruation or before the next period)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on triple divorce pronounced in a single session?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir and Imam Ali establishes the Shia doctrine of *Talaq al-Thalath fi Majlis* (triple divorce in one sitting), ruling that three pronouncements in a single session count as only one revocable divorce, contrary to the Sunni view of it being final. It cites the precedent of Ibn Umar and the practice of Imam Ali to demonstrate that the divorce is not binding until the woman marries another man, emphasizing the procedural fidelity to the Sunnah of one pronouncement per *Haidh* period.
